articlesStore.title: Ocean Voyager International Exports First Amphibious Craft from Sri Lanka
articlesStore.deck: Ocean Voyager International Exports First Amphibious Craft from Sri Lanka
articlesStore.body:
Ocean Voyager International (Pvt) Ltd, a yacht manufacturer based in Koggala, Sri Lanka has exported its first amphibious craft to Europe, a statement from the Ministry of Industries said.

Ocean Voyager International is known for producing luxury catamaran yachts. The firm was founded by Pierre Pringiers, a Belgian national who set up Sri Lanka's largest solid tyre manufacturing firm which was later bought by Michelin.

The amphibious launch has retractable motorized track systems on either side of its single hull which can be used to climb out of the water and move over solid ground.

Industries Minister Sunil Handuneththi who visited the yard to inspect the craft said the government would provide the required support to make Sri Lanka a boat – building hub.

Pringiers, who also chairs the Sri Lanka Leisure Yachting Group has been trying to promote the sector in an island which is surrounded by sea but, there is no active tradition of yachting. Sri Lanka's its marine economy is below potential analysts. (Colombo/Sept11/2026)

si.title: ඕෂන් වොයේජර් ඉන්ටර්නැෂනල් ශ්‍රී ලංකාවෙන් ප්‍රථම උභයජීවී යාත්‍රාව යුරෝපයට අපනයනය කරයි
si.deck: කොග්ගල පිහිටි ඕෂන් වොයේජර් ඉන්ටර්නැෂනල් සමාගම ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ නිපදවන ලද ප්‍රථම උභයජීවී යාත්‍රාව යුරෝපයට අපනයනය කළ බව කර්මාන්ත අමාත්‍යාංශය පවසයි.
si.body:
ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ කොග්ගල පිහිටි සුඛෝපභෝගී යාත්‍රා නිෂ්පාදන සමාගමක් වන ඕෂන් වොයේජර් ඉන්ටර්නැෂනල් (Ocean Voyager International Pvt Ltd) විසින් සිය ප්‍රථම උභයජීවී යාත්‍රාව (amphibious craft) යුරෝපයට අපනයනය කර ඇති බව කර්මාන්ත අමාත්‍යාංශය නිකුත් කළ නිවේදනයක දැක්වේ.

ඕෂන් වොයේජර් සමාගම සුඛෝපභෝගී කැටමරන් යාත්‍රා නිෂ්පාදනය සඳහා ප්‍රසිද්ධය. පසුව මයිකල් (Michelin) සමාගම විසින් අත්පත් කර ගන්නා ලද ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ විශාලතම ඝන ටයර් නිෂ්පාදන සමාගම ආරම්භ කළ බෙල්ජියම් ජාතික පියරේ ප්‍රින්ජියර්ස් (Pierre Pringiers) මහතා විසින් මෙම සමාගම පිහිටුවන ලදී.

මෙම උභයජීවී යාත්‍රාවේ තනි බඳෙහි දෙපසම මෝටර් බලයෙන් ක්‍රියාත්මක වන ඇදගත හැකි දම්වැල් ධාවන පද්ධතියක් (retractable motorized track system) සවිකර ඇති අතර, ඒ මගින් ජලයෙන් ගොඩබිමට පැමිණ ඝන පොළොව මත ධාවනය වීමේ හැකියාව පවතී.

යාත්‍රාංගනය නිරීක්ෂණය කිරීම සඳහා පැමිණි කර්මාන්ත අමාත්‍ය සුනිල් හඳුන්නෙත්ති මහතා ප්‍රකාශ කළේ ශ්‍රී ලංකාව බෝට්ටු හා යාත්‍රා නිෂ්පාදන කේන්ද්‍රස්ථානයක් බවට පත් කිරීම සඳහා රජය අවශ්‍ය සියලු සහාය ලබා දෙන බවයි.

ශ්‍රී ලංකා විනෝදාත්මක යාත්‍රා සංගමයේ සභාපතිවරයා ද වන ප්‍රින්ජියර්ස් මහතා, මුහුදෙන් වටවී තිබුණද යාත්‍රා පැදවීමේ සක්‍රීය සම්ප්‍රදායක් නොමැති දිවයිනක මෙම ක්ෂේත්‍රය ප්‍රවර්ධනය කිරීමට අඛණ්ඩව උත්සාහ කරමින් සිටී. ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ සාගර ආර්ථිකය එහි සැබෑ විභවයට වඩා බෙහෙවින් පහළ මට්ටමක පවතින බව විශ්ලේෂකයෝ පෙන්වා දෙති. (කොළඹ/සැප්11/2026)

ta.title: ஓஷன் வோயேஜர் இன்டர்நேஷனல் இலங்கையிலிருந்து தனது முதலாவது நீர்நில வாழ் ஊர்தியை ஐரோப்பாவிற்கு ஏற்றுமதி செய்கிறது
ta.deck: கொக்கலையில் உள்ள படகு தயாரிப்பு நிறுவனமான ஓஷன் வோயேஜர் இன்டர்நேஷனல், தனது முதலாவது நீர்நில வாழ் ஊர்தியை ஐரோப்பாவிற்கு ஏற்றுமதி செய்துள்ளதாக கைத்தொழில் அமைச்சு தெரிவித்துள்ளது.
ta.body:
இலங்கையின் கொக்கலையை தளமாகக் கொண்ட படகு தயாரிப்பு நிறுவனமான ஓஷன் வோயேஜர் இன்டர்நேஷனல் (Ocean Voyager International Pvt Ltd), தனது முதலாவது நீர்நில வாழ் ஊர்தியை (amphibious craft) ஐரோப்பாவிற்கு ஏற்றுமதி செய்துள்ளதாக கைத்தொழில் அமைச்சின் அறிக்கை ஒன்று தெரிவித்துள்ளது.

ஓஷன் வோயேஜர் நிறுவனம் சொகுசு கேடமரன் படகுகளை தயாரிப்பதில் புகழ்பெற்றதாகும். பின்னர் மிச்செலின் (Michelin) நிறுவனத்தால் வாங்கப்பட்ட இலங்கையின் மிகப்பெரிய திட டயர் உற்பத்தி நிறுவனத்தை அமைத்த பெல்ஜிய நாட்டைச் சேர்ந்த பியர் பிரிங்கியர்ஸ் (Pierre Pringiers) என்பவரால் இந்நிறுவனம் நிறுவப்பட்டது.

இந்த நீர்நில வாழ் ஊர்தியானது அதன் மேலோட்டின் இருபுறமும் உள்ளிழுக்கக்கூடிய மோட்டார் பொருத்தப்பட்ட ட்ராக் அமைப்புகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது, இதன் மூலம் நீரிலிருந்து வெளியேறி தரைப்பரப்பில் செல்ல முடியும்.

தளத்தை பார்வையிடச் சென்ற கைத்தொழில் அமைச்சர் சுனில் ஹந்துன்நெத்தி, இலங்கையை படகு கட்டும் மையமாக மாற்றுவதற்கு தேவையான ஆதரவை அரசாங்கம் வழங்கும் என்று தெரிவித்தார்.

இலங்கை பொழுதுபோக்கு படகு சவாரிக் குழுவின் தலைவராகவும் உள்ள பிரிங்கியர்ஸ், கடலால் சூழப்பட்ட போதிலும் படகோட்டம் பற்றிய பாரம்பரியம் இல்லாத இந்த தீவில் இத்துறையை மேம்படுத்த முயற்சித்து வருகிறார். இலங்கையின் கடல்சார் பொருளாதாரம் அதன் சாத்தியக்கூறுகளை விட குறைவாக உள்ளதாக ஆய்வாளர்கள் சுட்டிக்காட்டுகின்றனர். (கொழும்பு/செப்11/2026)

articlesStore.title: Sri Lanka state banks’ top bad loans exceed Rs200-bn; borrower names withheld under secrecy laws
articlesStore.deck: Sri Lanka state banks’ top bad loans exceed Rs200-bn; borrower names withheld under secrecy laws
articlesStore.body:
ECONOMATRIX — Sri Lanka’s state-owned Bank of Ceylon and People’s Bank account for more than 202 billion rupees in their top 20 non-performing loans, but borrower identities cannot be made public under statutory confidentiality rules, Parliament was informed. 
Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Anil Jayantha tabled details on the 20 largest non-performing loan (NPL) accounts across five state banks. Bank of Ceylon led with bad loans totaling 150,704.96 million rupees, followed by People’s Bank with 51,314.01 million rupees. 
Among the remaining institutions, National Savings Bank recorded 3,450.92 million rupees in its top 20 defaulted accounts, Regional Development Bank reported 1,214.33 million rupees, and the State Mortgage & Investment Bank accounted for 425.8 million rupees. 
Addressing requests to identify individual and corporate defaulters, Jayantha stated that financial institutions are bound by strict statutory privacy obligations. 
“Under Section 77 of the Banking Act and the Personal Data Protection Act, both boards and employees are legally bound to preserve customer confidentiality, so individual customer names have not been disclosed,” Jayantha said. 
Parliament was also provided details on some of the largest loans written off as bad debts or unpaid interest over the past 15 years across the five state institutions, evaluating only exposures exceeding one billion rupees. Under debt restructuring schedules, major write-offs at the Bank of Ceylon included 61 billion rupees tied to the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) restructuring—which was unbundled into six state-owned successor entities under the Sri Lanka Electricity Act No. 36 of 2024—alongside 15 billion rupees in real estate mortgages written off in 2017.
“The submitted reports reflect recovery determinations executed by the respective state banks pursuant to standard non-performing loan resolution mechanisms,” Jayantha said. 
Jayantha noted that while borrower identities remain protected by law, full figures and recovery proceedings have been tabled for parliamentary review.  (Colombo/Sep11/2026)

si.title: ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ රාජ්‍ය බැංකුවල ප්‍රධාන අක්‍රිය ණය රුපියල් බිලියන 200 ඉක්මවයි; රහස්‍යතා නීති යටතේ ණයගැතියන්ගේ නම් හෙළි නොකෙරේ
si.deck: ලංකා බැංකුව සහ මහජන බැංකුව ඇතුළු ප්‍රධාන රාජ්‍ය බැංකු පහේ විශාලතම අක්‍රිය ණය ප්‍රමාණය රුපියල් බිලියන 200 ඉක්මවා ඇති බවත්, බැංකු පනතේ රහස්‍යතා විධිවිධාන හේතුවෙන් ණයගැතියන්ගේ නම් හෙළි කළ නොහැකි බවත් පාර්ලිමේන්තුවට දැනුම් දෙයි.
si.body:
ඉකොනොමැට්‍රික්ස් — ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ ප්‍රමුඛ රාජ්‍ය බැංකු වන ලංකා බැංකුව සහ මහජන බැංකුව යන බැංකු දෙකෙහි විශාලතම අක්‍රිය ණය (non-performing loans) ගිණුම් 20 හි වටිනාකම රුපියල් බිලියන 202 ඉක්මවන නමුත්, ව්‍යවස්ථාපිත රහස්‍යතා නීති යටතේ එම ණයගැතියන්ගේ අනන්‍යතාව හෙළිදරව් කළ නොහැකි බව පාර්ලිමේන්තුවට දැනුම් දී ඇත. 

කම්කරු අමාත්‍ය සහ මුදල් හා ක්‍රමසම්පාදන නියෝජ්‍ය අමාත්‍ය අනිල් ජයන්ත මහතා රාජ්‍ය බැංකු පහක විශාලතම අක්‍රිය ණය ගිණුම් 20 පිළිබඳ තොරතුරු සභාගත කළේය. ඒ අනුව ලංකා බැංකුව රුපියල් මිලියන 150,704.96 ක අක්‍රිය ණය වාර්තා කරමින් ඉදිරියෙන්ම සිටින අතර, මහජන බැංකුව රුපියල් මිලියන 51,314.01 ක අක්‍රිය ණය වාර්තා කර ඇත. 

සෙසු ආයතන අතර, ජාතික ඉතිරි කිරීමේ බැංකුව (NSB) තම ප්‍රධාන පැහැර හරින ලද ගිණුම් 20 තුළ රුපියල් මිලියන 3,450.92 ක්ද, ප්‍රාදේශීය සංවර්ධන බැංකුව (RDB) රුපියල් මිලියන 1,214.33 ක්ද, රාජ්‍ය උකස් හා ආයෝජන බැංකුව (SMIB) රුපියල් මිලියන 425.8 ක්ද වාර්තා කර ඇත. 

තනි පුද්ගල හා ආයතනික ණය පැහැර හරින්නන් හෙළිදරව් කරන ලෙස කරන ලද ඉල්ලීම්වලට පිළිතුරු දෙමින් ජයන්ත මහතා කියා සිටියේ මූල්‍ය ආයතන දැඩි ව්‍යවස්ථාපිත රහස්‍යතා බැඳීම්වලට යටත්ව ඇති බවයි. 

“බැංකු පනතේ 77 වැනි වගන්තිය සහ පුද්ගලික දත්ත ආරක්ෂණ පනත යටතේ අධ්‍යක්ෂ මණ්ඩල සහ සේවකයින් යන දෙපාර්ශවයම ගනුදෙනුකරුවන්ගේ රහස්‍යභාවය සුරැකීමට නීතියෙන්ම බැඳී සිටින බැවින් තනි පුද්ගල ගනුදෙනුකරුවන්ගේ නම් අනාවරණය කර නොමැත,” ජයන්ත මහතා පැවසීය. 

පසුගිය වසර 15 තුළ රාජ්‍ය ආයතන පහ තුළ අකර්මන්‍ය ණය හෝ නොගෙවූ පොලී ලෙස කපා හරින ලද රුපියල් බිලියනය ඉක්මවන විශාලතම ණය පිළිබඳ තොරතුරු ද පාර්ලිමේන්තුවට ඉදිරිපත් කෙරිණි. ණය ප්‍රතිව්‍යුහගත කිරීමේ සැලසුම් යටතේ, ලංකා බැංකුවේ ප්‍රධාන කපාහැරීම් අතරට ලංකා විදුලිබල මණ්ඩලය (CEB) ප්‍රතිව්‍යුහගත කිරීමට අදාළ රුපියල් බිලියන 61 ක් සහ 2017 දී නිශ්චල දේපල උකස් සඳහා කපා හරින ලද රුපියල් බිලියන 15 ක් ඇතුළත් වේ. 

ණයගැතියන්ගේ අනන්‍යතාවය නීතියෙන් ආරක්ෂා කර ඇති නමුත්, සම්පූර්ණ සංඛ්‍යාලේඛන සහ අයකර ගැනීමේ ක්‍රියාමාර්ග පාර්ලිමේන්තු සමාලෝචනය සඳහා ඉදිරිපත් කර ඇති බව ජයන්ත මහතා වැඩිදුරටත් සඳහන් කළේය.  (කොළඹ/සැප්11/2026)

ta.title: இலங்கை அரச வங்கிகளின் முக்கிய வாராக்கடன்கள் ரூ.200 பில்லியனை தாண்டியது; இரகசியத்தன்மை சட்டத்தின் கீழ் கடன் பெற்றவர்களின் பெயர்கள் மறைப்பு
ta.deck: இலங்கை வங்கி மற்றும் மக்கள் வங்கி ஆகியவற்றின் முதல் 20 வாராக்கடன் கணக்குகள் ரூ.202 பில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமாக உள்ள போதிலும், சட்டப்பூர்வ இரகசிய விதிகளின் கீழ் கடன் பெற்றவர்களின் பெயர்களை வெளியிட முடியாது என நாடாளுமன்றத்தில் தெரிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.
ta.body:
இக்கொனோமேட்ரிக்ஸ் — இலங்கையின் அரசுக்கு சொந்தமான இலங்கை வங்கி (BOC) மற்றும் மக்கள் வங்கி (People's Bank) ஆகியவற்றின் முதல் 20 வாராக்கடன் கணக்குகள் 202 பில்லியன் ரூபாய்க்கும் அதிகமான தொகையைக் கொண்டுள்ளன, ஆனால் சட்டப்பூர்வ இரகசிய விதிகளின் கீழ் கடன் பெற்றவர்களின் அடையாளங்களை பகிரங்கப்படுத்த முடியாது என்று நாடாளுமன்றத்தில் தெரிவிக்கப்பட்டது. 

தொழில் அமைச்சரும் நிதி மற்றும் திட்டமிடல் பிரதி அமைச்சருமான அனில் ஜயந்த, ஐந்து அரச வங்கிகளில் உள்ள 20 மிகப்பெரிய வாராக்கடன் (NPL) கணக்குகள் பற்றிய விவரங்களை சமர்ப்பித்தார். இதில் இலங்கை வங்கி மொத்தம் 150,704.96 மில்லியன் ரூபாய் வாராக்கடன்களுடன் முன்னணியில் உள்ளது, அதைத் தொடர்ந்து மக்கள் வங்கி 51,314.01 மில்லியன் ரூபாயுடன் உள்ளது. 

மீதமுள்ள நிறுவனங்களில், தேசிய சேமிப்பு வங்கி (NSB) அதன் முதல் 20 கடனாளிகள் கணக்குகளில் 3,450.92 மில்லியன் ரூபாயையும், பிராந்திய அபிவிருத்தி வங்கி (RDB) 1,214.33 மில்லியன் ரூபாயையும், அரச அடமான மற்றும் முதலீட்டு வங்கி (SMIB) 425.8 மில்லியன் ரூபாயையும் பதிவு செய்துள்ளன. 

தனிநபர் மற்றும் நிறுவன கடனாளிகளை அடையாளம் காணுமாறு விடுக்கப்பட்ட கோரிக்கைகளுக்கு பதிலளித்த ஜயந்த, நிதி நிறுவனங்கள் கடுமையான சட்டரீதியான இரகசியத்தன்மை கடப்பாடுகளுக்கு உட்பட்டுள்ளன என்று கூறினார். 

“வங்கிச் சட்டத்தின் 77வது பிரிவு மற்றும் தனிப்பட்ட தரவுப் பாதுகாப்புச் சட்டத்தின் கீழ், வாடிக்கையாளர் இரகசியத்தன்மையைப் பேண பணிப்பாளர் சபைகளும் ஊழியர்களும் சட்டப்பூர்வமாக கட்டுப்பட்டுள்ளனர், எனவே தனிப்பட்ட வாடிக்கையாளர் பெயர்கள் வெளியிடப்படவில்லை” என்று ஜயந்த கூறினார். 

கடந்த 15 ஆண்டுகளில் ஐந்து அரச நிறுவனங்களில் வாராக்கடன்கள் அல்லது செலுத்தப்படாத வட்டியாக தள்ளுபடி செய்யப்பட்ட மிகப்பெரிய கடன்கள் பற்றிய விவரங்களும் நாடாளுமன்றத்திற்கு வழங்கப்பட்டன. கடன் மறுசீரமைப்பு அட்டவணைகளின் கீழ், இலங்கை மின்சார சபை (CEB) மறுசீரமைப்புடன் தொடர்புடைய 61 பில்லியன் ரூபாய் மற்றும் 2017 இல் தள்ளுபடி செய்யப்பட்ட 15 பில்லியன் ரூபாய் ரியல் எஸ்டேட் அடமானங்கள் ஆகியவை இலங்கை வங்கியின் முக்கிய தள்ளுபடிகளில் அடங்கும். 

கடன் பெற்றவர்களின் அடையாளங்கள் சட்டத்தால் பாதுகாக்கப்பட்டுள்ள போதிலும், முழுமையான புள்ளிவிவரங்கள் மற்றும் மீட்பு நடவடிக்கைகள் நாடாளுமன்ற ஆய்வுக்கு வைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளதாக ஜயந்த குறிப்பிட்டார்.  (கொழும்பு/செப்11/2026)

articlesStore.title: The Mechanics of Rupee Depreciation: Why Unsterilized Dollar Purchases Drain Sri Lanka’s Economy
articlesStore.deck: Central Bank dollar purchases created fresh rupee credit that boomeranged into import demand, weakening the rupee from 285 to 309 LKR per USD despite gross reserve accumulation.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon Special Dispatch) — LankaEcon News Desk

In the first half of 2025, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) purchased over $1.625 billion from the domestic foreign exchange market. Official press statements celebrated this achievement as evidence of external sector recovery and reserve accumulation. Yet, behind the headline reserve figure lies a fundamental monetary paradox: during this exact same period, the Sri Lankan Rupee depreciated from 285 to over 309 LKR per USD.

How can a central bank record massive dollar purchases while its national currency steadily loses value? 

The answer lies in the mechanics of unsterilized monetary expansion, a phenomenon first analyzed by central bank architect John Exter in 1949. When the central bank purchases $1.6 billion from commercial banks, it does not pay with pre-existing funds. It creates brand new, unbacked domestic rupees out of thin air and credits them into commercial bank settlement accounts.

If the central bank does not immediately "sterilize" this liquidity by selling down its holding of Treasury bills, this surge of fresh cash creates an artificial interbank liquidity surplus. Commercial banks, sitting on excess reserves, lower their lending standards and expand credit to importers. Within weeks, those newly created rupees hit the foreign exchange market to buy imported goods, driving dollar demand up and forcing the Rupee down.

articlesStore.title: The Soft-Peg Trap: How Standing Lending Injections Violate the Impossible Trinity
articlesStore.deck: Providing cheap overnight interbank liquidity below penalty rates fuels commercial bank credit expansion and forces central bank reserve drawdown.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon Special Dispatch) — LankaEcon News Desk

Central banking history in developing nations is littered with the remnants of the "Soft-Peg Trap." A soft peg occurs when a monetary authority attempts to maintain an exchange rate target while simultaneously managing domestic interest rates through discretionary market interventions.

In economic science, the Impossible Trinity (Mundell-Fleming paradigm) proves that no central bank can maintain three conditions at the same time:
1. A Fixed or Managed Exchange Rate
2. Free Movement of International Capital
3. An Independent Domestic Monetary Policy

When the Central Bank of Sri Lanka injected LKR 133.6 billion into commercial banks at 8.26%—well below the 9.25% Standing Lending Facility penalty rate—it attempted to suppress interbank interest rates artificially. Commercial banks used this cheap money to finance trade credit rather than attracting sticky deposits.

The predictable consequence unfolded rapidly: the cheap rupee credit spilled over into dollar conversion demand, forcing the central bank to intervene and sell precious foreign currency reserves to defend the exchange rate.

articlesStore.title: Why Import Restrictions Cannot Fix Current Account Deficits: The Savings-Investment Identity
articlesStore.deck: Banning motor vehicles and capital goods treats the symptom while fiscal budget deficits generate the excess rupee demand that spills into trade deficits.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon Special Dispatch) — LankaEcon News Desk

For decades, Sri Lankan policymakers have responded to foreign exchange shortages by imposing bans on motor vehicles, consumer goods, and agricultural imports. This mercantilist approach rests on a popular fallacy: the belief that trade deficits are caused by consumer greed and excessive purchasing of foreign goods.

Macroeconomic accounting reveals a far more fundamental truth expressed in the National Savings-Investment Identity:

Current Account Balance = National Savings minus Investment

When a government runs massive fiscal deficits funded by central bank money creation, it creates "dis-saving" in the public sector. This excess money spent by the state enters consumer hands, creating purchasing power unbacked by real production. Consumers naturally spend this excess money on both domestic and imported goods.

If the government bans imported cars, consumers do not save those rupees. Instead, they redirect the excess liquidity toward imported electronics, textiles, or food items. Banning specific import items simply shifts foreign exchange pressure from one sector to another without altering the net trade balance.

articlesStore.title: Reforming the Central Bank of Sri Lanka: From Discretionary Injections to Currency Board Rules
articlesStore.deck: David Ricardo’s 1816 Ingot Plan and John Exter’s 1949 warnings offer an imperative blueprint for anchoring long-term monetary stability.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon Special Dispatch) — By Disnaka

Sri Lanka's history since the establishment of the Monetary Law Act of 1949 has been marked by periodic balance-of-payments crises, severe inflation spikes, and currency devaluations. The core cause has always been discretionary central banking—the ability of monetary authorities to create money at will to monetize government debt or rescue over-extended banks.

To break this cycle, Sri Lanka requires structural monetary reform. David Ricardo’s 1816 Ingot Plan established that paper notes must be bound by strict convertibility rules to prevent over-issuance.

A modern Currency Board or rules-based monetary framework enforces two non-negotiable principles:
1. **100% Reserve Backing**: Every rupee issued must be backed 100% by foreign exchange reserves.
2. **Zero Deficit Monetization**: The monetary authority is legally prohibited from buying government Treasury bills or extending credit to commercial banks.

Under such a framework, inflation drops to world levels, exchange rate volatility disappears, and interest rates reflect true market savings.

articlesStore.title: The Three Master Visions of Money: Classical, Marxist, and Keynesian Lessons for Modern Sri Lanka
articlesStore.deck: Synthesizing David Hume, Karl Marx, and John Maynard Keynes clarifies why money printing cannot substitute for real national economic productivity.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon Special Dispatch) — By Disnaka

Economic history offers three distinct paradigms regarding the nature and role of money in human society:

1. **The Classical Vision (Hume, Smith, Ricardo)**: Money is a neutral "veil" that facilitates trade. Printing money does not create real wealth or real goods; it simply redistributes purchasing power and raises price levels proportionally.

2. **The Marxist Vision (Karl Marx)**: Money is the universal equivalent validating private labor. Money splits the act of sale from the act of purchase, creating the inherent possibility of hoarding, liquidity preference, and structural economic crises.

3. **The Keynesian Vision (John Maynard Keynes)**: Money is a store of value used to navigate fundamental uncertainty. In the short run, prices and wages are "sticky," meaning monetary shocks can affect real output and employment.

Understanding modern macroeconomics requires recognizing that Keynesian sticky-price dynamics dominate in the short run (over weeks or months), but Classical long-run monetary neutrality holds true in the long run. Printing rupees to fund government spending may briefly cushion shocks, but over time it yields pure inflation and currency depreciation.

articlesStore.title: Overtrading Without Deposits: How Interbank Liquidity Windows Distort Commercial Banking in Sri Lanka
articlesStore.deck: When commercial banks rely on cheap central bank liquidity facilities instead of attracting sticky customer deposits, credit expansion outpaces real savings.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon Special Dispatch) — By Disnaka

A healthy banking sector relies on sticky customer savings deposits—from household thrift and corporate earnings—to fund long-term loan portfolios. However, when central banks offer cheap overnight standing lending windows, commercial banks fall into the habit of "overtrading."

Overtrading occurs when commercial banks grant aggressive loans first and search for funding later, relying on central bank liquidity windows to balance their daily clearing accounts.

This operational distortion undermines financial stability in two ways:
1. **Moral Hazard**: Commercial banks stop competing aggressively for long-term customer deposits because cheap central bank liquidity is always available.
2. **Artificial Credit Cycles**: Loan expansion outpaces real national savings, creating asset bubbles and eventual credit contraction when central bank injections are withdrawn.

Prudential regulation must enforce strict penalties on standing facility usage, ensuring that interbank liquidity serves as a true "lender of last resort" rather than a permanent source of cheap loan funding.

articlesStore.title: Sri Lanka Central Bank Keeps Policy Rates Unchanged Amid Stabilizing Inflation Trajectory
articlesStore.deck: The Monetary Policy Board noted that current interest rate structures remain aligned with target inflation corridors while fostering private sector credit transmission.
articlesStore.body:
COLOMBO (LankaEcon) — The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has decided to maintain the Standing Deposit Facility Rate (SDFR) and the Standing Lending Facility Rate (SLFR) at their current levels of 8.25 percent and 9.25 percent, respectively.

The decision was reached at the Monetary Policy Board meeting following a comprehensive review of domestic and global macroeconomic developments. The Board observed that the prevailing monetary policy stance continues to be appropriate to anchor inflation around the target corridor of 5 per cent over the medium term.

"Private sector credit expansion has demonstrated encouraging momentum across agricultural, manufacturing, and services sectors," stated CBSL Governor in the official policy announcement. "Liquidity conditions in the domestic money market remain comfortably positive, ensuring uninhibited interest rate transmission across commercial banking channels."

Gross official reserves reached $6.1 billion at the end of the previous month, bolstered by worker remittance inflows, tourism receipts, and official multilateral discursions under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) program.

Market participants on the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) reacted positively to the announcement, with banking sector counters rallying in early morning trading.

econArticlesStore.title: Exchange Rate Overshooting & The Purchasing Power Parity Paradox in Island Economies
econArticlesStore.authorTitle: Senior Macroeconomics Fellow & Professor of Economics
econArticlesStore.authorAffiliation: University of Colombo Faculty of Economics
econArticlesStore.summary: An empirical examination of short-term currency volatility against long-term inflation differentials and central bank market liquidity interventions in small open island economies.
econArticlesStore.content:
Abstract: Short-term exchange rate adjustments in open developing economies frequently deviate from traditional Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) equilibrium models due to sticky price adjustments, capital flow shocks, and central bank foreign exchange reserve interventions.

1. Executive Overview & Theoretical Background
The dynamics of floating exchange rate regimes in South Asia present complex theoretical and policy challenges. When central bank policy interest rates are adjusted, foreign exchange markets absorb capital flow expectations long before domestic goods market price levels adjust.

2. The Dornbusch Overshooting Framework
In the short run, nominal exchange rates move beyond their long-run equilibrium level in response to monetary policy shocks. This overshooting phenomenon explains why currency depreciations in small open island economies often trigger temporary real exchange rate misalignments before equilibrium is re-established.

3. Empirical Findings & Central Bank Liquidity Implications
Data spanning 2015–2025 demonstrates that unhedged commercial bank FX swap positions exacerbate speculative overshooting. When the Standing Deposit Facility Rate (SDFR) is held below market expectations, private sector capital flight accelerates nominal exchange rate depreciation.

4. Policy Recommendations
• Establish automated central bank foreign exchange auction corridors to absorb panic liquidity.
• Maintain market-determined interest rate spreads to anchor inflation expectations.
• Enhance gross official foreign reserve adequacy to at least 4.5 months of import cover.
keyTakeaways: Short-term currency swings are driven by financial expectations rather than immediate trade balances.
Sticky prices in domestic goods markets create temporary real exchange rate misalignments.
Central bank reserve buffers reduce speculative overshoot volatility.

econArticlesStore.title: Sovereign Debt Restructuring & Comparability of Treatment: Lessons for Sri Lanka
econArticlesStore.authorAffiliation: Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) & CBSL Research Advisory
econArticlesStore.summary: Analyzing haircut parameters, net present value (NPV) debt reductions, official bilateral creditor coordination, and macro-linked bond mechanisms in sovereign debt workouts.
econArticlesStore.content:
Abstract: Sovereign debt workouts under the G20 Common Framework require delicate alignment between official bilateral creditors (Paris Club and non-Paris Club) and private international bondholders (ISBs).

1. Introduction
Sri Lanka's 2022 sovereign debt default marked a watershed moment for middle-income developing nations navigating complex multi-creditor debt restructuring.

2. Comparability of Treatment (CoT) Mechanism
The principle of Comparability of Treatment ensures no creditor group receives preferential financial terms. Calculating Net Present Value (NPV) reductions across varied debt instruments—such as official bilateral loans, commercial bank credits, and sovereign Eurobonds—requires standardized discount rate benchmarks.

3. Macro-Linked Bonds (MLBs) & State-Contingent Payouts
The inclusion of Macro-Linked Bonds ties debt service obligations directly to real GDP growth trajectories. If real GDP exceeds baseline IMF targets, bondholders receive upside coupon adjustments; conversely, downside economic shocks trigger debt service relief.

4. Conclusion & Fiscal Policy Imperatives
Maintaining primary fiscal surpluses above 2.3% of GDP is indispensable to anchor debt-to-GDP ratios below 95% over the medium term.
keyTakeaways: Comparability of Treatment prevents free-riding by commercial Eurobond holders.
Macro-Linked Bonds align debt service obligations with national economic growth capacity.
Primary fiscal surplus targets are essential to achieve debt sustainability parameters.

econArticlesStore.content:
Abstract: Disentangling supply-side import cost shocks from demand-side monetary expansion is critical for central bank policy interest rate calibration.

1. Theoretical Framework
Milton Friedman’s classic dictum that 'inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon' must be qualified in small open island economies dependent on imported food, fuel, and fertilizer.

2. Monetary Transmission vs Energy Price Spikes
Empirical impulse response functions demonstrate that currency depreciation and global oil price surges account for 60% of short-term CPI inflation spikes, while net domestic assets (NDA) expansion of the central bank fuels sustained medium-term core inflation.

3. Central Bank Independence & Monetary Board Governance
The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) Act No. 16 of 2023 legally prohibits direct primary market monetary financing (money printing) for government budget deficits, establishing flexible inflation targeting (FIT) as the sole legal mandate.

4. Policy Recommendations
• Target core inflation within the 3%–5% corridor via the Standing Deposit Facility Rate.
• Strengthen domestic supply chain resilience to buffer external food and energy price shocks.
keyTakeaways: Supply shocks trigger immediate price level shifts, whereas monetary expansion drives sustained inflation trends.
Legal prohibition of deficit monetization is pivotal for central bank credibility.
Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) anchors long-term inflation expectations.
